responses.reply:
Got it — extending retention for the support export, keeping the existing purge mechanism and deployment process untouched.

One consequential gap: "retain longer" isn't a number, and the approved security policy caps retention at 30 days (current is 7). The purge job already accepts a numeric retention value, so this is really just picking that number.

What retention period do you want — and is it driven by a specific investigation-window requirement (e.g., "investigations typically take X days to open"), or just "as long as policy allows" (30 days)?

responses.spec:
[Extend Support Export Retention]

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v1
Frozen: true
Type: Engineering
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Target retention period: 14 days | Decided: user, acting as the approved security policy owner, set the value to 14 days and explicitly authorized it as within the 30-day limit | None — value is within policy ceiling and explicitly authorized by the policy owner. | resolved |
| D2 | Reuse existing purge implementation and deployment process unchanged | Decided: user explicitly stated "keep the existing purge implementation and deployment process," reaffirmed as "leave everything else unchanged" | None — purge job is already tested and takes a numeric retention value; only the parameter changes. | resolved |
| D3 | Retention ceiling is 30 days | Observed: approved security policy permits at most 30 days retention | None — 14 days is within this ceiling. | resolved |
| D4 | Longer retention's exposure-window tradeoff is accepted | Decided: user, as security policy owner, authorized 14-day retention with full knowledge it extends the exposure window beyond the current 7 days; no additional mitigation requested | Check: no separate mitigation task exists; if exposure profile changes materially, revisit with the policy owner. | accepted-uncertainty |

## Decision History

_No superseded decisions._

## Critique Reconciliation

| Finding ID | Source / specification version | Disposition | Reason / incorporated change |
|---|---|---|---|

## Problem Statement

Investigations into support issues currently have only 7 days of transcript history available before the scheduled purge removes exports, which is insufficient for some investigations. The organization's approved security policy permits retaining these transcripts for at most 30 days.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Support export retention period increased from 7 days to 14 days | A 13-day-old transcript remains present after purge; a 15-day-old transcript is purged. Verified via the existing, already-tested purge job's test suite run against the new 14-day parameter. | D1, D2, D3 |

## Constraints

- Retention value must not exceed 30 days (approved security policy) — D3. 14 days satisfies this.
- No changes to the purge implementation or deployment process — D2.

## Success Criteria

- Purge job configured with a 14-day retention parameter.
- A transcript aged 13 days is retained; a transcript aged 15 days is purged, confirmed by the existing purge test suite.

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests

- Existing purge job test suite, run with retention parameter = 14, asserting: 13-day-old transcript present after purge run; 15-day-old transcript absent after purge run.

### Regression Checks

- Existing purge job test suite (unchanged logic, new parameter value) serves as the regression check — no new test infrastructure needed.

### Failure Signals

- A 15-day-old transcript surviving a purge run, or a transcript younger than 14 days being purged, indicates a parameter or off-by-one failure.

### Verification Methods

- Run existing automated purge test suite with the updated parameter; no manual verification required given existing coverage.

### Feedback Loop Design

- One-time verification at deployment of the new parameter value via the existing test suite; no new recurring check introduced beyond the already-scheduled purge job's normal operation.

### Known Blind Spots

- Test suite covers the boundary transcripts (13-day, 15-day) but the spec does not specify additional edge cases (e.g., exactly 14-day-old transcript); left to the existing test suite's established boundary convention since no new test infrastructure is introduced.

## Inputs

- Current retention setting: 7 days (Observed).
- Policy ceiling: 30 days (Observed).
- Existing, tested, scheduled purge job accepting a numeric retention value (Observed).
- New target retention value: 14 days (Decided, D1).

## Outputs

- Updated retention parameter value (14) supplied to the existing purge job configuration.

## Out of Scope

- Changes to the purge implementation itself (D2).
- Changes to the deployment process (D2).
- Interface changes (per task framing — no interface decision needed).
- New mitigations for the extended exposure window (D4, accepted-uncertainty).

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide

- Mechanical details of where/how the 14-day value is set in existing configuration, provided the purge implementation and deployment process remain unchanged.

### Executor Must Escalate

- Any retention value exceeding 30 days (violates approved security policy).
- Any need to modify the purge implementation or deployment process to achieve the change.

### Executor Must Not Change

- The purge implementation or deployment process (D2).
- The retention value beyond 14 days without new authorization from the policy owner.

## Current Interpretation

Extend the support export retention period from 7 days to 14 days, authorized by the security policy owner and within the 30-day policy ceiling, by updating the numeric parameter passed to the existing, already-tested, scheduled purge job. No changes to the purge implementation, its deployment, or any interface. Success is verified via the existing purge test suite confirming a 13-day-old transcript is retained and a 15-day-old transcript is purged.

## Misclassification Risks

### Potential False Positives

- A test passing only because it checks the wrong boundary (e.g., 14-day-old transcript) rather than the specified 13/15-day boundaries; mitigated by requirement's explicit boundary values.

### Potential False Negatives

_[open — none identified beyond blind spot above]_

## Ambiguities

### Blocking

_None remaining._

### Non-Blocking

_None identified._

### Intentional

- D4: exposure-window tradeoff from longer retention is knowingly accepted by the policy owner without additional mitigation.

## Risks

- Retaining transcripts for 14 instead of 7 days modestly increases the exposure window if export storage is compromised — explicitly accepted by the policy owner (D4).

## Stakeholders

- Support/investigations team (beneficiary of longer retention).
- Security/compliance owner of the 30-day policy ceiling (user, who authorized this change).</spec>
